key_insight: DVM-HALL reframes loyalty for autonomous commerce by modeling brand choice as a recursive human-agent loop that combines human preferences, agentic utility, trust, delegated authority, and verifiable execution.
engineering_relevance: The framework is relevant for designing auditable AI commerce systems, especially in DeFi and tokenized loyalty settings where execution risk and traceability materially affect agent decisions.
method: Softmax brand-choice model with human emotional equity, machine-experience utility, trust, delegation, and verifiable execution terms.
Recursive updating of trust and delegation after each interaction to capture dynamic human-agent adaptation.
NHAS metric to audit alignment using feedback, execution logs, benchmark comparisons, and verifiable receipts.
evidence_signal: The abstract proposes a three-stage validation plan: controlled shopping experiments, multi-agent market simulations, and DeFi testbeds.
watch_item: The model may be difficult to deploy reliably because real-world execution risks, smart-contract vulnerabilities, and noisy human feedback can make NHAS calibration unstable.
paper_title: The Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) Model and the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS) in Autonomous Commerce
